title: How John Rush built 26 AI products in 3 years bootstrapped with a 50/50 co-maker model
summary: John Rush explains his bootstrapped playbook: build an audience in public, sell before building, ship a tiny MVP with no-code tools, and split 50/50 with a technical co-maker. He also covers directories, AI agents, automating toward one-button tools, and staying productive by skipping unimportant work.

principles.text: Validate by sharing the idea publicly, then sell it manually to ~10 people before building anything.
principles.quote: I just don't even build the tool I do the job myself like I'm the tool and then I sell that to around 10 people to validate whether people are willing to pay for that or not.

principles.text: Keep teams tiny: split 50/50 with a co-maker who codes, and hire no one until ~50k MRR.
principles.quote: We hire no more people until we hit at least 50k MR and only then we probably hire some people.

principles.text: Build in public: marketing becomes a byproduct of your process, and you launch to an audience already waiting.
principles.quote: the marketing was a byproduct of you sharing your own process. So there's no extra special marketing you have to do on top of it.

principles.text: Focus on one social platform until about 4-5k followers, then expand to all platforms.
principles.quote: get somewhere to 4k or maybe 5k followers and then go everywhere like all 10 platforms stack LinkedIn everything else.

principles.text: Start with the audience, not the product: try to sell first, perfect the pitch, then build a simple MVP.
principles.quote: I start with the audience and then I go back and get to the product. You have to figure out whether you can build the audience for this because you will have to build the audience once you launch.

principles.text: Don't spend effort on unimportant things early; put almost all effort into the pitch, and use templates.
principles.quote: don't do anything that's not important yet. Just put 1% effort, get something out, don't care. Be embarrassed.
